content.title: About
content.content: Red Enchilada Sauce (4501) is a traditional Mexican sauce made from tomatoes, chilies, garlic and spices. It delivers a bright, mildly spicy flavor with smoky undertones and is used as a base for enchiladas, tacos and burritos.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: The sauce is named after the Mexican dish “enchilada,” where it is poured over the filling.
Classic recipes use dried ancho and chipotle chilies, giving it a distinctive smoky aroma.
Red sauce is often prepared in advance and can be kept in the refrigerator for several weeks.
In the United States it ranks among the top‑10 best‑selling sauces in the Mexican cuisine category.

items.title: Rich in lycopene
items.content: Tomatoes provide lycopene, a powerful antioxidant that supports heart health.

items.title: Contains vitamin C
items.content: Vitamin C boosts immunity and aids iron absorption.

items.title: Low in fat
items.content: Unlike creamy sauces, red enchilada sauce contains virtually no saturated fat.

items.title: Source of capsaicin
items.content: Chilies add capsaicin, which may boost metabolism and have anti‑inflammatory effects.

items.title: Spicy food
items.content: The chili content can irritate the stomach of individuals sensitive to spicy foods.

items.title: Tomato allergy
items.content: Some people may experience allergic reactions to tomatoes or the spices used.

items.title: Sodium content
items.content: The sauce can be salty; those monitoring sodium intake should watch portion size.

content.title: How to Use
content.content: Serve the sauce hot as a topping for enchiladas, casseroles, chili con carne, or use it as a dip for nachos and as a marinade for chicken or fish.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep the sauce in a sealed container in the refrigerator for up to 4 weeks. After opening, it can be frozen in portions for up to 3 months. Discard if the smell or color changes.
